title: GST Return Reconciliation (GSTR-2B vs Books)
summary: Match GSTR-2B and 2A data against the purchase register invoice by invoice, find ITC at risk before GSTR-3B is filed, and draft supplier follow-ups for approval.

seo.title: GSTR-2B vs Purchase Register Reconciliation | VipraTech
seo.description: AI reconciliation of GSTR-2B and GSTR-2A against the purchase register: normalised invoice matching, ITC-at-risk reports and supplier follow-ups.

problem.intro: Before filing GSTR-3B each month, someone downloads GSTR-2B for every GSTIN and compares it with the purchase register. Input tax credit depends on suppliers reporting invoices correctly, so differences in invoice numbers, GSTINs, dates or tax heads turn directly into credit that is deferred, reversed or questioned later in an ASMT-10 scrutiny notice or a DRC-01C intimation.

pain_points.title: Invoice numbers never match exactly
pain_points.detail: INV/24-25/0045 in the books is 45 or INV0045 in GSTR-2B, so lookups fail and juniors match lines by eye.

pain_points.title: Volume across GSTINs and clients
pain_points.detail: Firms run this for many clients and registrations against the same monthly deadline, and the reconciliation gets squeezed.

pain_points.title: Supplier follow-up is manual
pain_points.detail: Emails to suppliers who missed GSTR-1, used the wrong GSTIN or reported the wrong period are drafted one by one and tracked in a spreadsheet.

pain_points.title: Decisions are not recorded
pain_points.detail: When a notice arrives months later, it is hard to show why credit was claimed or deferred for a particular invoice.

solution.overview: We build a GST reconciliation engine that takes GSTR-2B and, where needed, GSTR-2A files for each GSTIN, downloaded from the portal or fetched through your GSP, and reconciles them against the purchase register from the books. It normalises invoice numbers, GSTINs, dates and tax heads, then matches in passes: exact, normalised invoice number, value and date within tolerance, and one-to-many for split or consolidated invoices. Where only invoice PDFs exist, the document layer extracts the fields first. Every line lands in a category, such as matched, value mismatch, in books but not in 2B, or wrong GSTIN. The accountant decides ITC treatment, and supplier follow-ups are drafted for approval.
capabilities: Imports GSTR-2B and GSTR-2A JSON or Excel files per GSTIN, plus purchase register exports
Invoice-number normalisation for prefixes, financial-year tags, separators and leading zeros
Tolerance-based matching on taxable value, IGST, CGST and SGST split, and invoice dates
Extracts fields from purchase invoice PDFs where the register is incomplete
Categorised mismatch report with ITC-at-risk summary by supplier
Drafts supplier follow-up emails and carries open items into the next month

workflow.title: Load 2B and the purchase register
workflow.detail: GSTR-2B files for each GSTIN and the purchase register for the same period are imported side by side.

workflow.title: Normalise fields
workflow.detail: Invoice numbers, GSTINs, dates and tax heads are cleaned so formatting differences do not block matches.

workflow.title: Match in passes
workflow.detail: Exact, normalised, tolerance and one-to-many passes run in order, each match tagged with the rule that produced it.

workflow.title: Review mismatches
workflow.detail: Low-confidence matches and mismatched lines go to the tax associate, who confirms the category.

workflow.title: Decide ITC and follow up
workflow.detail: The GST manager decides whether credit is claimed, deferred or reversed, and approves supplier emails.

workflow.title: Report for GSTR-3B
workflow.detail: An ITC working and supplier-wise open items are produced for return preparation and carried forward.

compliance_notes: Under GST, input tax credit generally depends on the supplier reporting the invoice so that it appears in the recipient's GSTR-2B; the tool helps you evidence that check, while eligibility decisions stay with the tax professional.
The decision log supports replies to scrutiny notices by showing what was matched, by which rule, and who decided.

faqs.q: Do we need GSP or API access to the GST portal?
faqs.a: No. The engine works with GSTR-2B and GSTR-2A files downloaded from the portal. If you already use a GSP, we can fetch the same data through it to save the download step.

faqs.q: How does it deal with different invoice number formats?
faqs.a: It normalises prefixes, financial-year tags, separators and leading zeros before matching, then applies amount and date tolerances you set for each client. Every match shows which rule produced it.

faqs.q: Can it file GSTR-3B or claim ITC for us?
faqs.a: No. It prepares the reconciliation and the ITC working. The decision to claim, defer or reverse credit and the filing itself stay with your team.

faqs.q: We handle many clients. Is data kept separate?
faqs.a: Yes. Each client and GSTIN is a separate workspace with its own access controls, tolerances and history, so carry-forward items and decisions never mix across clients.
